fun_facts: Chuba Hubbard is from Sherwood Park, Alberta, Canada.
As a child, Chuba Hubbard set Canadian records in the 100- and 200-meter races with the Edmonton Olympic Track and Field Club.
As a teenager, Chuba Hubbard ran the 100 meters in 10.60 seconds at the 2015 World Youth Championships—the fourth-fastest time in his age group.
In 2019, Chuba Hubbard rushed for 2,094 yards, second only to Barry Sanders' legendary Oklahoma State season, and tied Sanders with 12 100-yard games.
Chuba Hubbard was named AP Big 12 Offensive Player of the Year and finished eighth in Heisman Trophy voting.
Chuba Hubbard won the Cornish Trophy, awarded annually to the top Canadian player in NCAA football.

As if the Carolina Panthers didn’t have enough open-field juice in their offensive backfield with [Christian McCaffrey](https://www.nfl.com/players/christian-mccaffrey) ﻿, the club added a home-run hitter Saturday in selecting Oklahoma State running back [Chuba Hubbard](https://www.nfl.com/players/chuba-hubbard) in the fourth round of the 2021 NFL Draft with overall pick No. 126.

What Hubbard brings to the NFL foremost is speed -- a world-class sprinter as a teenager, he once clocked the world’s fourth-fastest time in his age group in the 100-meter dash (10.60 seconds) at the IAAF World Youth Championships in 2015.
